```sql
WITH tenant_customers AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.email,
           c.company,
           c.country_code
      FROM customers c
     WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
),
agg AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
      JOIN tenant_customers tc ON tc.id = o.customer_id
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
    HAVING max(o.created_at) >= %(from)s
       AND max(o.created_at) <  %(to)s
)
SELECT tc.id,
       tc.email,
       tc.company,
       tc.country_code,
       a.revenue,
       a.order_count,
       a.last_order_at
  FROM agg a
  JOIN tenant_customers tc ON tc.id = a.customer_id
 ORDER BY a.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orders worden nu eerst gejoind met alleen de klanten van de gevraagde tenant, in plaats van alle orders te materialiseren en voor alle klanten te aggregeren. Totalen, aantal en laatste orderdatum komen uit één aggregatie (`max(created_at)` vervangt de `DISTINCT ON`-sortering), en het datumfilter staat in `HAVING`. Ik filter bewust via `customers.tenant_id` en niet via `orders.tenant_id`, zodat de resultaten identiek blijven aan het origineel.
